newsitem.title: USA: N.J. towns approve revised school budgets -- paper.
newsitem.headline: N.J. towns approve revised school budgets -- paper.

text.p: Several New Jersey townships approved revised school budgets to comply with a state deadline set on districts where voters had previously rejected spending plans, the Philadelphia Inquirer reported Tuesday.
The Monroe, N.J., Township council agreed to $1.5 million of cuts to the school district's budget, the newspaper said.
The cuts are slightly below the $1.8 million originally proposed after voters rejected an $11.1 million budget and $2.5 million supplemental spending plan on April 15.
Collingwood's Board of Commisioners adopted an $8.3 million budget that will reduce the local purpose tax rate by about four percent.

In Medford, officials last week approved a revised budget cutting the tax rate increase by 0.57 cents. Medford's proposed $23 million budget vote resulted in a tie at the ballot box April 15, which under state law is considered a defeat.
Riverside officials voted to cut the school district's $10.2 million budget by $79,800. Riverside's original budget lost by two votes on April 15.
